newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Cyclone Rachel to pass close to Port Hedland.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Cyclone Rachel to pass close to Port Hedland.

text.p: Winds with gusts of up to 180 kilometres per hour are expected to pass close to the coastal community of Port Hedland around 0400 GMT (12.00 p.m.) as cyclone Rachel makes its way down the coast of Western Australia, the Bureau of Meteorology said on Tuesday.
A warning for a category three cyclone is current for coastal areas between the towns of Wallal and Onslow, including Dampier, Wickham, Roebourne, Karratha and Port Hedland, the bureau said.
At 2200 GMT (6.00 a.m.), Rachel was 110 km north northeast of Port Hedland and 270 km east northeast of Karratha.
The cyclone is moving southwest at 15 km per hour toward Port Hedland, the bureau said.
Destructive winds with gusts up to 180 km per hour are expected near the cyclone center, the bureau said.
Gales, with gusts up to 120 km per hour are expected in the remainder of the warning area east of Karratha, extending to Onslow on Tuesday night or early on Wednesday, the bureau said.
Heavy rains are expected to cause local flooding, the bureau said.
A category three cyclone carries winds of between 170 km and 224 km per hour.
Oil and gas producing operations potentially in the path of Rachel were making plans late on Monday to halt production and evacuate the regions.

Non-essential personnel were evacuated on Monday from both Barrow and Thevenard islands, where a combined 40,000 to 45,000 barrels of oil are pumped daily in preparation for a shut down, a spokesman for West Australian Petroleum Pty Ltd (WAPET) said on Monday.

The Cossack Pioneer offshore rig, with daily ouptut from the North West Shelf of around 90,000 and the 70,000 bpd Griffin oil field were both making plans on Monday to disconnect and leave the cyclone region, spokesmen for the operations said on Monday.

WAPET is a joint venture of Texaco Inc, Chevron Inc and Royal Dutch/Shell Group, each with two-sevenths stakes, and Mobil Corp, with one-seventh. Equal partners in the North West Shelf project are units of The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, British Petroleum Co Plc, Japan Australia LNG (MiMi) Pty Ltd, a partnership of Mitsui & Co Ltd and Mitsubishi Corp, Chevron,
Royal Dutch/Shell and Woodside Petroleum Ltd.
